ENT Clinical Note – Dr Smith / Matt Carter (DOB 14 Aug 1989)

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • 6-week history of feeling “tired, run-down” with diffuse musculoskeletal aching.  
  • Preceded by U.S. holiday with frequent hiking in shorts; possible environmental tick exposure.

- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Well through Dec / early Jan.  
  • Returned from U.S. late Jan; symptoms began ~2 wks later (mid-Feb).  
  • Single annular rash on back of calf appeared mid-/late Feb, faded over ~2 wks.  
  • Fatigue, reduced appetite (no weight change) and generalized aches have persisted since.

- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat: mild sore throat only at time of rash; none currently.  
  • No throat-tightness/closure sensation, no dysphagia/odynophagia, no drooling.  
  • Voice: no hoarseness/voice change.  
  • Nasal/ocular: baseline allergic rhinitis only (hay fever).  
  • Breathing: no dyspnea, stridor or wheeze; asthma stable.  
  • Swelling: none of lips, tongue, uvula, face, joints.  
  • Ear/neck: no ear pain/hearing change; no neck pain or swelling.

- Relevant past episodes/treatments:
  • None similar previously; no prior ED visits or epinephrine use.

- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug/food allergies: not documented.  
  • Medications:  
    – Inhaled corticosteroid (preventer) – dose/route AM & PM (exact inhaler not documented).  
    – OTC oral antihistamine – dose/frequency not documented.  
    – No rescue inhaler use recently.

- Social context:
  • Lives with wife; able to work but with reduced effectiveness.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: none reported or seen; prior calf rash resolved.  
- Airway/breathing: no distress, no stridor.  
- Mental status: alert, oriented; concentration reduced by fatigue.  
- Vitals / exam: Not recorded.  
- Accompaniment: consultation conducted remotely; patient alone at time of call.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression: Suspicion of early disseminated Lyme disease presenting with constitutional symptoms and prior erythema-migrans–like rash.
  Evidence: outdoor exposure in endemic area, annular calf rash, temporal relation to onset of fatigue/arthralgia.

- Differential diagnosis (from DDx, consistent with transcript):
  1. Lyme disease – high likelihood; classic rash, timeline, outdoor exposure.  
  2. Post-viral fatigue (e.g., EBV/CMV) – moderate; sore throat and prolonged fatigue, but rash atypical.  
  3. Hypothyroidism – consider; fatigue/myalgias common, will screen (no specific stigmata).  
  (No conflicts noted between DDx and transcript.)

Plan:
- Investigations ordered: blood panel including Lyme serology, CBC, renal & liver function, thyroid profile, inflammatory markers.  
- Patient instructed to book phlebotomy via support line and arrange follow-up tele-consultation ~1 week after blood draw.  
- Education / red-flags: seek urgent care if new fever, spreading rash, facial weakness, palpitations, breathing or swallowing difficulty, joint swelling or neurological symptoms develop.  
- Asthma/hay-fever: continue preventer inhaler and antihistamine as usual; resume regular exercise as tolerated.  
- No immediate pharmacologic treatment initiated; antibiotics to be considered if Lyme serology positive.  
- Follow-up: telephone review of results; consider ENT or infectious-disease referral if diagnostic uncertainty or symptom progression.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: complete allergy list, full medication names/doses, vital signs, detailed physical examination (including oropharyngeal & cervical nodes), auto-injector status (for asthma/allergy).  
● Conflicts between transcript & DDx: none identified.  
● Transcript quality: clear overall; minor audio dropouts but did not affect clinical content.
